Appendix 2: Various other Varmams

It may also be mentioned that the Tamil varma sastra speaks of certain other marma situated in the anatomical area once discussed above they are discussed below. 184

Yenthi varmam is positioned 5 cms. Below the Thivalai varmam on either side of the rib cage. The Yenthi varmam located on the left side is known as left yenthi varmam and the one on the right side yenthi varmam. This has got this name because with this point we can hold the whole body. The victim of this varmam disorder will suffer form tetanus. The patient will becomes weak and lose his hearing power. Within 3 hours the patient should be attended to, for cure. Kaikkoottu varmam is situated at the opposite side (back side) of the Yenthi varmam. If Kaikkoottu varmam is affected, then the ball and the socket of the shoulder joint will be affected. The patient will faint and his hands will be raised. The tongue will stammer and tetanus will set in. The patient should be treated within four hours of disorder of this life-centre. Kutthu varmam, Ulkutthu varmam, Pulpatru varmam, Kurukku varmam, all these four life centres (varmams) points are situated on the back. Thoosi varmam, Thoosika varmam, Thudi varmam, Pidi varmam (Idi varmam), Kanal 185

varmam (Kazhalai varmam), Valai varmam, Eelai varmam (Kulai varmam), Vil varmam, Hanumaar varmam, all the above nine life centres are situated around the nipples of both the breasts. In males these varma points are easy to locate but in female they cannot be located easily. These life centres are situated above the lungs and hence are very sensitive. The lungs will get affected once these life-centres are inflicted. Fainting, blood vomiting, thirst, constipation and retention of urine are observed in patient who has disorders of this life-centre. Occurrence of tuberculosis and hunch-back are other symptoms. The limbs of the patients will also get affected. The patient who is affected with the impact of these life-centres is to be attended within three hours, failing which death due to blood vomiting will occur. Ari varmam point is situated two inches below the Koombu varmam. The damage to Ari varmam will lead to reddening of the eyes, fainting and tetanus and the patient will coil himself into a bundle and will gasp and shout in pain. 186

The patient has to be treated within seven hours and thirty minutes of the varma disorder. Mundellu varmam is situated on the floating ribs on both sides. In case Mundellu life-centre is inflicted, the intestine will get affected. The patient will have diarrhoea, fever and shivering cough and fainting are also likely to occur. Saruthi varmam is of two types. One is Munsaruthi varmam and the other Pinsaruthi varmam. The Munsaruthi varmam is positioned 7 cms. Above the Mundellu varmam. Pin saruthi varmam is situated 2 cms. above Munsaruthi varmam. These two life centres are found on either side of the body. If these life centres are disturbed, tetanus, stomach pain, cramps, and swelling of the body will occur. Pain and breathing difficulties will also be experienced. Below the waist shivering will occur. Numbness of legs will set in. Pallai varmam is situated on either side of the umbilicus. The affected person will bend. Air (vayu) will rise up. The victim will experience giddiness. 187

The patient should be attended to within seven hours of the occurance of impact to this lifecentre. Surukku varmam resides adjacent to Mundellu varmam. Both motion and urine will be retained once surukku varmam is disturbed. Pain in the legs will occur. In course of time, other sufferings will arise. Kareeral varmam life-centre resides in the liver (kareeral). Owing to this varma disorder, the patient's radial artery below the thumb will be pronounced in appearance. The patient will be restless, and his body will stretch, and in due course bend like a bow. Further this disorder reflects the signs and symptoms of Thoosika varmam. The patient should be treated within three hours of the varma disorder. Kaikkatti varmam life centre is situated 8 cms. Below the Thummi varmam. This is situated near adaipu varma on the front of the shoulder. This is termed as Allumel Adaipu Kaikoottel in Varma kannadi. Odimurivu (32) calls it Varma mada Adappathil Kaikettu and located at the shoulder joint. 188

Brahmma varmam is otherwise named as Annakkala varmam or Undhi varmam or Aamendra varmam or Ayan varmam. If Brahma varmam is affected, the patient will have running nose giddiness, writhing of the body, weakness in the limbs and closing of eyes. The body will become reddish and the patient will bleed through the anus and mouth. Seminal discharge will be observed and the stomach will bloat. The patient will have much problem within seven hours of being affected. The patient should be treated within one hour. Valampuri varmam is situated 2. 5 cms. on the right side of the penis. Damage to Valampuri varmam leads to retention of urine of urine and motion, stomach upset, numbness in the limbs and pricking pain in the penis. Within seven hours of the impact of this life-centre, the patient should be treated. Idampuri varmam is located 2. 5 cms. on the left side of the penis. Damage to Idampuri varmam shows the same signs and symptoms observed for Valampuri varmam. In addition, pain in the penis and body-ache will occur. 189

Villurumi varmam is situated near the Valampuri varmam. If Villrumi life centre (varmam) is affected due to any impact. The lower part of the abdomen becomes numb. The victim will become weak. Body pain, giddiness, fever and pain in the lower part of the abdomen and mental confusion will also occur. Vallurumi varmam resides near idampuri varma point. If affected by impact at Vallurumi varmam, the signs and symptoms will generally be the same as that of the Vallurumi varmam. The disorder of Vallurumi varmam should be treated within seven hours. Narankukutthi varmam is located in the groin between the genital region and the anus. If affected the patient back will have giddiness, breathlessness, loss of speech and swelling of the body. If the damage is severe, patient will die. Ani varmam which is also called Melani varmam. Ani varmam is situated 10 cms, above the Narankukutthi varmam, 2.5 cms. above the male genital organ. 190

Involuntary discharge of semen will be the symptom of this varma disorder. Anthai varmam is Location d 2.5 cms. above the Melani varmam. If this varmam is damaged, the patient will become unconscious quite often. Like this, the victim will suffer. Swasam adappan is seen in the mid axillary line at the level of the two nipples. If injured the patient patient complaints stretching sensation of the nerves fainting frothy discharge from the mouth. Nooluvalippan is situated three and a half inches above the nipples. On injury lead to congestion of chest with phlegm. Froth from the mouth, stiffness in both hands. This ewill lead to Rajayakshma. Urulumani marma are seen even below the malapandam near the testicles. If injured this will cause fainting and the two testicles ascends towards the nabhi and get itself lodged there. Give pressure over two angula below the anal region and also gently press over the navel and bring these testicles downwards. 191

Study of Katikataruna Marma

Etymology Katikataruna—Katika taruna is a combination of two words Kati and taruna. The word Kati is derived from Kat dhatu which means that which is clothed Taruna is referred in this context as soft or cartilage. Description These marma are situated on both the sides of the vertebral column corresponding to the

posterior aspect of the ilium. These are two in number and are Asthi marmas. They are Kalanthara pranahara and of half anguli in extent. Its bhuta structure is Agni and Jala. Adhidevatha is Roudra. An injury to any of this Katikatharuna (Sacroiliac articulation) situated in the region of sroni (Sacrum) on both sides of the spinal column, gives rise to excessive pain, hemorrhage and consequent pallor and ends in death. 1,2 Fractures of this bone may affect the important pelvic organs and cause death due to complications such as pallor, anaemia and emaciation. It is suitable to consider the marma near the upper margin of pelvic bone which form the Kati and few centimetre away from the lumbosacral joint. Study of Nitamba Marma

Nitamba Etymology—The word nitamba is derived from tamu dhatu. This prefixed by ni pratyaya. Tamu means Glani and also Kamksha. As after sexual act the part which is tired first is Nitambha. In the second context it is said that the males derive urge for sex after seeing this part. Description Situation of the marma is above the sroneekandam (pelvic girdle) and both the sides of the vertebral column. Injury to this marma leads to the atrophy of the lower limb and endangers life in course of time. They are two in number, these are asthi marmas and also Kalanthara pranahara. It is half anguli in extent. Its bhuta structure is Agni and Jala. Adhidevatha is Raudra. Surface Anatomy The examination of this marma is preferably done in patients lying on chest and abdomen. The nitamba marma lies on half the distance between sacral bone and the greater trochanter of 198

Study of Kukundara Marma

Kukundara Etymology—The word Kukundara is derived from the word Kundara which is prefixed by the word Ku. Ku is usually used to denote nindyartha as in Kuprasidhi, Kutsitha, down, notorious. Kukundara means Omal Kuzhi or a small depression near the buttocks. Description Situation of these marmas is on both sides of vertebral column, corresponding to the sacroiliac articulation anterior to which the Sciatic nerve passes. Injury to this marma leads to complete anesthesia and inability to use the lower extremity. They are two in number and are sandhi marmas, at the same time they are vaikalyakara also. They are half anguli in extent. Its bhuta structure is Soumya. Adhidevatha is Raudra. Surface Anatomy The Kukundara marma falls within the pelvic cavity. The palpation of the marma can be started as stated for the katikatharuna simultaneously with both hands/ by tracing the margin of sacral bone on both sides. It is possible to feel the tenderness on the line. 195

Another statement of Susruta Parswayor Jaghana bahir bhaga Dalhana comments. Parswa as vama and Daksina bhaga. 196

Among the 14 prishta marmas, Kukundara marma is the only marma that comes under the sandhi classification. On deep dissection one may find this area Sacro iliac articulation. Symptoms of injury narrated in various Ayurvedic texts are so vivid and complete, that nothing need to be added or deleted from the text even now. Sparshajnana paraplegia. □ Chesta Hani = loss of motor activity o Sensory loss. Both clubbed together lead to complete Tamil varma sastra According to the varma sastra four fingers below the ullellu varma lies Pinnellu varma. The symptoms are whole body swelling, irritant and prolonged cough, sore throat. Accumulation of phlegm in the chest, fever with vomiting. Start treatment within 7 nazhigai. Arasa varma is situated little below the pinnellu adjacent to the spinal cord. Injury causes fever, irritable bowel, weakness and numbness over the extremities. 197

Start remedial measures immediately. Internal medicines should be started only after 51 Nazhikai.

Study of Amsaphalaka Marma

Amsaphalaka Etymology—This is the combination of two word Amsa and Phalaka. This literally means flat surface near the shoulder. These are two in number and are sira marmas and kalanthara pranahara also. It is of half anguli in extent. Its bhuta structure is Agni and Jala. Adhidevatha is Iswara. Injury to these marmas leads to continuous bleeding and endangers life in course of the time due to complications. Surface Anatomy This marma apparently falls near the kidney located inside. Beneath this point are arterial branches of the kidney are located. However these parts are not palpable superficially on the back. It is easier to probe these marma with the thumbs simultaneously on the sides of thoracic vertebrae (8th- 9th). Injury to this marma causes collection of blood in the abdominal cavity and causes danger of life. Injury to this marma (Coeliac axes) which are situated medially below the extremities of the side (Parsva), and which lies attached at the middle between the loins fills the koshta with blood and results in death. They are sira marma two in number and half anguli in extent. Its bhuta structure is Agni and Jala. Adhidevatha is Rudra. Surface Anatomy This point falls between the two parsva, urah and koshta parsva (Parshavanta rapratibadhau), and also the point falls above the pelvic girdle (Jaghana). The vertical area drawn from the region of axilla on the iliac spine, passes through the region of Parsva. The sandhi is the junctional area of the two 201

Yenthi varmam is positioned 5 cms. below the Thivalai varmam on either side of the rib cage. The Yenthi varmam located on the left side is known as left Yenthi varmam and the one on the right side Yenthi varmam. The victim of this varmam disorder will suffer form tetanus. The patient will becomes weak and lose his hearing power. Within 3 hours the patient should be attended to, for cure. The location of Kondakolly marma is in between the axilla and the hip inside the rib cage. If injured he should be immediately manipulated by pressing the Orkarathu marma in the lower limb. Or this injury could be manipulated by pressing the opposite side. 203

Appendix 3: Various other Varmam

Sadappira varmam is otherwise known as Ananda Sadappira varmam. Below the navel adjacent to the nadusurukki lies the Sadappira. Sadappira varmam is situated on the back exactly opposite to the kaikkaatti varmam on either sides. Sada means the dead body. Persons affected with varma resemble like a dead body. The victim will be dazed and his eyes will be open once Sadappira life centre is disturbed. Tiredness and pain all over the body are other symptoms. This disorder should be attended to within six hours of its occurrence. Kilippura varmam are two, varmas situated 2.5 cms. above the sadappira life-centre. Kilippira is described as Kilimegha in Varma Kannadi. The face will be distorted on one side. Motion will be blocked. The patient will laugh, and not be able to speak. 214

It is preferably be treated within seven hours of the on set of the disorder for cure. Kilimega varmam life centre is found 5 cms. above the Kilippura varmam, which is 5 cms. below the shoulder blade on the back According to Varma Suttiram this is in the hip region 4 fingers above the sadappira varma. If the Kilimega life-centre is affected the weak person will lose his consciousness within one and half hours. The patient will make sound like a parrot. Tears in the eyes will also be seen. The victim should be treated within four hours. Kilippura varmam and kilimega varmam are located on either side of the body. These two lifecentres are together called as poonool varmam. Poonool life centre is situated on both sides of the shoulders bone on which the holy thread (poonool) is normally worn. If Poonool varmam life-centre is affected, the patient will lose his consciousness, and the limbs will lose activities. Continuous coughing and tetanus are also seen. The patient will have nightmares. 215

There are difference of opinion regarding the position of the Nettellu varmas. Some say that these are two fingers above the Pallavarma which is located at the depression of the mundellu. There are 32 vertebrae in the backbone. In this column, there are eight life centres and a collective name for these eight life centres is Nettellu varmam. They are situated one below the other. Nettellu varmam I (Mel Suzhiyaadi varmam) is situated 11cm. from top of the head. That is positioned at the beginning of the spinal column. The affliction of Mel suzhiyaadi life centre leads to loss of appetite, tuberculosis, fever, shivering and itching at the top of the spinal column. The controlling nerve will lose its strength. If the impact at the life centre is serious, the person will become insane. It should be treated at the earliest. Nettellu varmam II resides 7 cms. below the nettellu varmam - I If this varmam sustains damage, the symptoms will be worse than the previous varma disorder. The patient vomit blood. Nettellu varmam III is situated 7 cms. below the Nettellu varmam II. - - 216

If affected, the patient will have fever and cough. His testicles will ascend into the abdomen. After two hours there will be heavy breathing and the patient faint. Frothing at mouth will also occur. Nettellu varmam - IV is situated 7 cms. below nettellu varmam III which is more or less in the centre of the back. varmam In case disorder occurs to Nettellu IV the patient will have hunch back and burning micturition. The patient will become weak and have tuberculosis. The senses will function below normal and heavy coughing will obstruct speech. Nettellu varmam V is situated 4 cms. below the centre of the back. Damage to the life centre reveals symptoms similar to poisoning. Further giddiness, tiredness, sweating, dryness of the mouth, stomach pain, painful urination and constipation will appear. The patient should be rubbed with the special medicated oil (Sarvaanga thailam). Still the patient is likely to expire on the 648th day. Nettellu varmam VI is situated 7 cms. below the Nettellu varmam V - 217

If Nettellu varmam - VI is affected the patient will feel tired, giddiness and blurring of vision. Nettellu varmam - VII is located on the two depressions found just over the buttocks. Excretion of urine and motion, as well as dislocation of hip bones are the symptoms which reveal the affliction of this life-centre. Nettellu varma - VIII is otherwise called Kaikatti varmam or Keezh suzhiyadi varmam. Nettellu varmam VIII is positioned at the coccyx bone. In case of its disorder, the patient will faint and froth at the mouth. He will be totally disabled. Even if treated he will have abdominal disturbance. Pain in the chest, dysentery (kirani), vomiting, tuberculosis etc. will also occur. The patient will become a mental wreck. seven hours. The patient is to be attended to within Kachchai varmam is situated slightly below the Nettellu varmam. If affected the patient will have pain in the legs. He will have retention of urine and motion. If the symptoms do not appear initially, the same will be 218

seen later. Irritation at the thoracic region will arise due to gastritis and chest pain. Kaikkootti varmam is located 7 cms. below the adappa varmam. The patient will faint and have breathing difficulties once this life-centre is affected with impact. Pain in the ribs and limbs will be felt. There will be blood stain in the saliva and stomach ache with the stretching of body. The urine will drip continuously. The patient should be treated within seven hours of the disorder to this life-centre; otherwise it is difficult to cure. Vasaukkala. Vaasikkala is otherwise named Vaasikkala varmam resides on the sharp points of the vertebrae. There are sixteen such points situated on all the vertebrae. These are on the reverse sides also. 219

Amsa Etymology—The word Amsa has a various range of meaning starting from Shoulder, a A marma, □ Amsha, □ Yudha. Description There are two marmas seen situated on either side midway between the neck and the head of the arms and connects the amsa peetha and skandha (Shoulder). An injury to any of these marma can lead to incapacity of moving the hands. They are two in number and are snayu in origin and they are vaikalyakaram also. It is of half anguli in extent. Its bhuta structure is Jala. Adhidevatha is Iswara. Surface Anatomy This marma is located on the amsa which is formed by the union of amsa peetha (glenoid) and the Skanda (acromioclavicular). This is found on either side of the shoulder. Probe the index finger on acromion protuberance and glide the finger slowly towards the base of the cervical triangle. The patient will faint and the head will sink once this life centre is disturbed. The neck will be affected and the patient will at times vomit blood. The body will jerk and the patient will have muscle cramps on the arms and legs. The pulse will be at low ebb. The treatment should be given within four hours of impact at the life centre. Otherwise the damage will be permanent and loss of life may occur. Some times the patient's head will sink permanently and the affected side will also be paralyzed. Bhuja varmam rests at the tips of the collar bones on either side. In other words, each upper arm has a Bhuja varmam. The victim of this disorder, will not be able to lift the hands freely. The area will become numb and swelling will set in. The patient will not have a wink of sleep and will become faint. The patient should be attended to within one and half hours. Vilangadi varmam (vilangu varmam) which is otherwise called Vilangu varmam is situated at the point where the collar bone and the shoulder bone meet on the front side of the body. 212

In case the Vilangu life-centre is affected the victim cannot lift his arms. Fainting giddiness and fever will arise. Sulukku varmam is otherwise called Kaaraikkuzhi varmam. Sulukku varmam is located at the meeting of collar bone and the shoulder bone at the sides. If disorder occurs to Sulukku life-centre, the middle finger will be affected because the nerve running down the arm will be affected. Hence the name Sulukku varmam. This varmam is found on either side of the shoulders. Sulukku varma disorder will make the patient lose consciousness, will produce protruding of tongue and twisting of the neck. The impact to sulukku varmam (nerve centre) should be attended to within seven hours of disorder. Kulayana marma Kulayana marma adds one more marma in this position. Phanam is a marma seen inside the armpit. If injured the patient faints. He could be 213

Injury to this marma causes much pain and endangers life in course of time of complication. (P. V. Krishna Rao) 226

Conclusion

CONCLUSION Ayurvedic medical knowledge is not to be practised by doctors alone but also by warriors as well. Charaka Sutrastana Ch 30. There were two schools of thought regarding marma that existed in India. They were 1. Ayurvedic, 2. Tamil Varma. These systems, though mainly developed for different reasons, their theory basically remained the same. Hence it is clear that the difference between these are more semantic than substantial. Changing a few terms, the corpus knowledge of each system can be translated into the other, thereby widening the scope of each. These two systems had its own merits and demerits. The marmas which were enumerated in Ayurveda was basically meant for surgeons to skillfully avoid these areas during areas during the surgery. The exact location, area, structure and prognosis of each and every marma were very widely dealt with. There is also little or no difference in opinion regarding the marmas on number, area, site between the different authors. But here, less attention were paid in the treatment aspects of marmabhighata. The treatment

modalities were totally missing which makes this science incomplete. Even the naming of marma was done with a specific reason and rationale. Injury to this varma can be successfully treated only when the complete knowledge on quality and location is obtained. In Tamil varma sastra there are many treatise which deals with this art. Numerous manuscripts are collected at various centres in India. A theoretical text is fairly meaningless without a teacher who knows the practical skills himself. A vital spot at any part of the body could be identified only with the help of a experienced teacher. Even if the spot is identified the way it should be stimulated or revived also need to be taught from a guru. Each and every practitioner has developed this science into his area of understanding that to a novice, it has become extremely difficult to have a standardised approach. Though the practitioners of this science agree in unanimity regarding the total number of varma which they claim to be 108, there is difference of opinion regarding the name, size, position and prognosis. A detailed table regarding the identification 271

and terminology of around 25 paduvarmam and 295 thoduvarmam are given in appendix II. Kulayana system of practise is meant for warriors to afflict the maximum possible injury in combat. These tradition has already developed a lineage in trauma care that even now it is in par with the modern orthopedics. The treatment modalities of trauma care, Immobilisation, bandage techniques, and physiotherapy methods like massage, exercises all need proper documentation and unbiased study. Based on this anatomical exposition of the marmas, surgeonshould take a cue and try to conclusively establish the truth of Susruta's wisdom that the marmas are structural complexes in the human body best avoided during surgery. Similarly it is worthwhile to study the nature of fractures, haemorrhages, gynaecological problems and sports injuries with refernce to the knowledge embodied in the study of marma, and also to ascertain whether the marma could be used for anaesthetic purposes. Veterinary doctors could also try to find use for the study of marmas in animals as narratted in Hasthyayurveda or Aswayurveda. 272

On a wider range, alternate therapy practitioner like Reiki, Pranic healing and professional masseurs could benefit by the study of marmas. In fact the marma as a complete folk medical practise could be developed by refining its diagnostic and treatment methods. The pharmacopia as in Siddha system could also be standardized and made scientifically more acceptable. Epilogue "The perfection of knowledge depends upon the investigation of things" Confusius The above statement of the greatest philosopher of all times reveals the little known scientific temperament of the multi faceted personality. Since the perfecting of knowledge depends upon, investigation, critical analysis and unbiased assessment we have ventured to examine in detail the anatomy of marma as envisaged in the two. Efforts have been made to offer scientific explanation to the general observation and accurate exposition of the ancient seers. Yet there remain main concepts to be explained It is pity that the concept of Marma Adankal, Amritha kala and so on are still shrouded 273

with mystery. The need of this hour is to, make consolidated efforts to revive, and revitalise the science by all possible means. In this age of sophistication where electronic gadgets that can quantify and transform the intricate physiological activities like heart beat vision sleeping pattern in ECG, ERG, EMG, efforts should be made to graphically represent and quantify various nadi patterns, SO that the identification, no longer remains in the realms of subjective feeling and assessment but on quantifiable data and tangible proof. A symbolic relationship between compatible therapies of the east and west would go a long way in the overall development of various systems. Even within this country there exists certain isolated pockets of traditional knowledge which have to be identified and embraced onto the main stream. A judicious admixture of traditional wisdom and, modern scientific exposition using the latest technology innovation, investigatory techniques and the updated knowledge on anatomy and physiology is very much in the need. In brief let us endeavour to do what confusious asked us ages ago. "Let us perfect the knowledge by investigation" 274
